title: Statistical Methodology
purpose: Seed statistical method selection and interpretation so Lantern can inspect a hypothesis/design/dataset, choose appropriate analysis families, evaluate assumptions and sample adequacy, and interpret uncertainty/effect size without confusing significance with truth or importance.

concepts.definition: A structured collection of observations with provenance, variables, units/measurement definitions, sampling/selection process, scope and missingness information.
The population quantity/effect the analysis intends to estimate; method choice should follow the estimand/question.
A numerical summary of observed data such as mean, median, variance, quantile, rate or proportion.
A rule/procedure that maps sample data to an estimate of an estimand.
Estimated sampling variability of an estimator under a specified model/design.
An interval generated by a procedure with stated long-run coverage under assumptions; not generally a posterior probability that a fixed parameter lies in the realized interval.
A quantitative measure of magnitude/difference/association relevant to the scientific question.
A decision/test property relative to a null model, statistic and threshold; not a measure of practical importance or theory truth.
Under a specified null model and analysis plan, probability of data/test statistic at least as incompatible with the null as observed; not P(null is true).
Probability that a specified testing procedure rejects a null/achieves a criterion when a specified alternative/effect is true under assumptions.
Selecting sample size from desired precision/power, effect size of interest, variability, design and error criteria before data collection where applicable.
Inference comparing one sample/estimate with a reference value/distribution.
Inference comparing two groups/samples with paired/independent structure explicitly represented.
Observations linked within units/matched pairs; analysis should preserve dependence.
Samples whose observations are independent across groups under the design/model.
Methods for proportions/counts/categories, including contingency structures.
A model relating an outcome to one or more predictors/covariates under explicit functional/distributional assumptions.
A method relying on fewer/different distributional assumptions than a corresponding parametric model; not assumption-free.
Conducting multiple inferential tests creates increased false-positive/discovery risk requiring explicit control/interpretation.
Analysis used to discover patterns/generate hypotheses; flexible but not independent confirmation of hypotheses generated from the same data.
Analysis evaluating prespecified hypotheses/estimands/plans or using independent/held-out evidence.
Whether an estimated magnitude matters for the real decision/scientific context, distinct from statistical detectability.

guards.reason: A p-value conditions on the null model; it is not the posterior probability the null is true.
Very small effects can be statistically detectable, especially with large samples.
Non-significance may reflect low power, uncertainty or small effects; absence/equivalence requires appropriate analysis.
Large samples reduce some random error but do not repair bias, confounding, dependence or invalid measurement.
Small samples generally increase uncertainty/power limitations; they do not make observations automatically false.
Assumptions depend on the model/statistic/residual structure, not a blanket normality rule.
Nonparametric methods still rely on sampling, independence, ordering/exchangeability or other assumptions.
Statistical association does not establish causal identification.
Regression becomes causal only under an appropriate causal design/identification assumptions.
The same exploratory data cannot independently confirm the pattern it generated.
Standard frequentist coverage is a property of the procedure over repetitions, not generally a posterior probability statement.
Power describes detection performance under specified alternatives; it does not validate measurement/design or truth.

invariants: Statistical method selection begins with the scientific question/estimand, study design and data structure.
Paired/dependent and independent observations must be distinguished.
Effect magnitude and uncertainty should be interpreted together.
Statistical significance, effect size, practical significance and causal evidence are separate.
Sample size affects uncertainty/power but cannot substitute for methodological validity.
P-values are not probabilities that hypotheses are true.
Non-significant results do not automatically establish no effect.
Exploratory discoveries require held-out/independent evidence for independent confirmation where feasible.
Exact numerical analysis belongs to deterministic quantitative code; this package defines selection, assumptions and interpretation.

provenance.authoring_basis: Core statistical inference/method-selection principles across experimental and observational research, adapted to Lantern's deterministic quantitative-organ boundary.
